articles.title: Some Mount Vesuvius victims suffered slowly and one victim’s brain turned to glass, new research says
articles.summary: The remains of those who became trapped by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius tell a story of tragic suffering, according to a new analysis of their bones.
articles.body: The remains of those who became trapped by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius tell a story of tragic suffering, according to a new analysis of their bones. On August 24 in the year 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried cities like Pompeii, Oplontis and Stabiae beneath ash. Pompeii was preserved by the volcanic ash and has become a unique archaeological site. But mudflows and giant, sweeping clouds of hot, toxic gas and volcanic matter destroyed the wealthy coastal town of Herculaneum. The site is near what is now known as Naples in Italy. In a cruel twist of fate, the residents of Herculaneum were able to see the eruption and actually tried to escape its destructive path by evacuating on boats along the waterfront. “Herculaneum is interesting because of its position,” said Tim Thompson, study author and professor of Applied Biological Anthropology at Teesside University in England. “It gives a snapshot into the way in which these people responded and reacted to the eruption, which you do not get at Pompeii.” But the beach and vaulted stone boathouses became the final resting place for hundreds of residents. Many of those who died on the beach were adult or young adult men, and a significant number of those who died in the boathouses included women and children. The boathouses, known as fornici, were first discovered in 1980. Three separate excavations of the vaulted spaces have revealed the remains of at least 340 people. They became trapped in the boathouses when volcanic clouds swiftly descended on the town, likely moving as rapidly as 62 to 186 mph (100 to 300 kilometers per hour), according to previous research. Initially, researchers believed that the skin and soft tissue of the people were vaporized by the heat, initially estimated to reach between 572 and 932 degrees Fahrenheit. That vaporization would have killed them instantly. But a research team decided to re-examine the skeletons using new bone analysis techniques to determine how they died. Their findings published Thursday in the journal Antiquity. The researchers discovered that the bodies had not been exposed to the high temperatures expected with the volcano’s pyroclastic flow, or massive cloud of toxic gas and material. Based on their study of the ribs from 152 of the skeletons, and the discovery of collagen still within the bones, the temperatures they faced stayed below 752 degrees Fahrenheit. Collagen gelatinizes into a jelly-like substance above 932 degrees Fahrenheit. Bone structure changes in response to heat due to its mineral content, which exists in the form of tiny crystals. And more collagen remained in the bones than expected. “The heat causes some changes externally, but not necessarily internally to the bones,” Thompson said. “What was interesting was that we had good collagen preservation but also evidence of heat-induced change in the bone crystallinity. We could also see that the victims had not been burned at high temperatures.” The boathouses also helped keep the harshest of the heat from reaching them. Unfortunately for Vesuvius’ victims, that means they lived long enough to be baked alive in the stone boathouses while suffocating from toxic fumes, according to the researchers. “Although these people died, it wasn’t through instant soft tissue vaporization,” Thompson said. “They hid for protection and got stuck. The walls of the fornici, as well as their own body mass, dispersed the heat in the boathouses, which more closely relates to baking.” Glass brain In a separate study published this week in the New England Journal of Medicine, researchers analyzed a Vesuvius victim’s skull and found the remains of a brain that had been vitrified, or turned into a glass-like substance by the heat. The remains were also recovered in Herculaneum, and belonged to a person found lying facedown on a wooden bed that was buried by volcanic ash, according to the study. The bones were charred from the intense heat the person suffered after the eruption. Although the remains were found in the 1960s, the glass-like remnants? of the person’s brain were recently uncovered in the skull. They found a glassy black substance, and further investigation revealed that it included several proteins associated with brain tissue, along with adipic and margaric fatty acids found in sebum and hair. These were not found in any of the surrounding material at the site. Charred wood enabled them to determine that temperatures reached 968 degrees Fahrenheit at the site. The researchers believe that the extreme heat ignited the person’s body fat, vaporized soft tissue and vitrified the fatty proteins of the brain. The researchers noted that the preservation of brain tissue at such old sites, or the vitrification of it, is incredibly rare. The only other past instance of this they could find for comparison happened to victims of firestorms during World War II. “Considering the discovery of vitrified brain remains from a victim of the 79 AD Vesuvius eruption, it may be of some interest to the scientific community to open a discussion on the process of vitrification occurring in human remains,” the researchers wrote.

articles.title: NI secretary and PM 'stand full square behind' Good Friday Agreement
articles.summary: Sir Chris Bryant clarifies comments made by the prime minister on Thursday that a border poll is "off the table".
articles.body:
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant has said he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham "stand full square" behind all of the Good Friday Agreement, including its provisions for a border poll.

During his first visit to Northern Ireland on Thursday, Burnham said a border poll was "off the table" and that votes on Brexit and Scottish independence showed the "risks that come from those situations take a long time to heal".

However on Friday, Sir Chris said the point Burnham was making was that discussions for a border poll were "not on the table" during discussions on Thursday.

"He was not making a general statement about the whole future of the Good Friday Agreement," Sir Chris said.

Burnham met Stormont's first and deputy first ministers and the leaders of the Northern Ireland Assembly's main parties during the visit.

He said the focus should be on public services and tackling cost-of-living pressures.

The Good Friday Agreement, also known as the Belfast Agreement, was a political deal designed to bring an end to 30 years of violent conflict in Northern Ireland, known as the Troubles.

It was signed on 10 April 1998 and approved by public votes in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

It set up a new government for Northern Ireland, representing both nationalists and unionists.

The agreement says that Northern Ireland is part of the UK and this can change only through a referendum.

The secretary of state must hold a border poll if it appears likely that a majority of people in Northern Ireland would vote for Irish unification.

There is no detail in the agreement on how the secretary of state should judge whether there is majority support - but they can decide to hold a border poll at any time, provided that there has not been another in the last seven years.

There is also debate as to what form a border poll should take, for example whether the poll should be held on the general principle of unification or after specific proposals have been set out for how a united Ireland would be governed.

Thursday's visit came amid calls from the Northern Ireland's power-sharing executive for increased funding from the government to ease budget pressures.

The four-party coalition has yet to set a budget nearly five months into the financial year.

Stormont departments are facing a shortfall of up to £1.6bn , according to a spending watchdog.

On Friday, Sir Chris acknowledged the financial pressures in the executive, but he said there needed to be "some financial discipline".

"Whatever the envelope is, however big it is, and we may be able to help to some degree, you still have to live within that overall envelope," he told BBC News NI.

"That means we've got to set a budget for this year, there's got to be some savings, some self-help, some revenue raising over the years ahead."

He said he wanted to have a discussion with executive ministers about "reform of the system" and setting a budget for the next couple of years so that there is "some degree of stability".

articles.title: MC Pipokinha: show foi ao lado de escola durante horário letivo | G1
articles.standfirst: Apresentação que terminou em condenação ocorreu em área aberta durante a tarde e ficou visível para estudantes de uma escola próxima. Decisão foi julgada em 1ª instância e cabe recurso.
articles.summary: Apresentação que terminou em condenação ocorreu em área aberta durante a tarde e ficou visível para estudantes de uma escola próxima.
articles.body:
Alunos de uma escola de Corumbá , a cerca de 420 quilômetros de Campo Grande, conseguiram assistir à apresentação de MC Pipokinha que resultou na condenação da cantora por danos morais coletivos, aponta o Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul (MPMS). A decisão foi julgada em 1º instância e ainda cabe recurso. Assista vídeo acima.

O g1 entrou em contato com as defesas de Pipokinha e dos outros quatro réus, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O show ocorreu durante a tarde de 16 de fevereiro de 2023, em um trio elétrico instalado em uma área aberta do município, com ampla visibilidade para pessoas que estavam nas proximidades, incluindo estudantes que estavam em aula.

De acordo com o MPMS, vídeos apresentados no processo comprovaram que a cantora ficou parcialmente nua durante a apresentação e realizou simulações de atos sexuais no palco.

Segundo o MPMS, a apresentação ocorreu em local aberto e amplamente visível a transeuntes e a alunos de uma escola próxima, em pleno horário letivo.

O Ministério Público sustentou que a situação expôs crianças e adolescentes, inclusive estudantes na faixa dos 14 anos, a conteúdo impróprio e atos considerados obscenos.

A condenação decorre de uma Ação Civil Pública ajuizada pelo MPMS contra a artista, dois dançarinos e os organizadores do evento.

Pipokinha em publicação recente em apresentação — Foto: Redes Sociais

Na decisão, o juiz Maurício Cleber Miglioranzi Santos, da 1ª Vara Cível de Corumbá, entendeu que o conteúdo apresentado ultrapassou, naquele caso, os limites da liberdade artística.

Para o magistrado, os organizadores deveriam ter adotado medidas para impedir que crianças e adolescentes fossem expostos ao conteúdo. A sentença também considerou que o tipo de apresentação era previsível diante do histórico conhecido da artista contratada.

A Justiça reconheceu a existência de dano moral coletivo e levou em consideração a gravidade dos fatos, a presença de adolescentes, a exposição da apresentação em local aberto e o potencial de prejuízo causado pela situação.

MC Pipokinha, apontada na ação como a principal responsável pela apresentação, foi condenada a pagar R$ 100 mil.

Outros quatro envolvidos na realização do evento foram condenados ao pagamento de R$ 15.525 cada. Ao todo, as indenizações somam R$ 162,1 mil.

O valor deverá ser destinado ao Fundo Municipal dos Direitos da Criança e do Adolescente de Corumbá (FMDCA).

O Ministério Público havia requerido a condenação solidária dos réus ao pagamento de indenização por danos morais coletivos de, no mínimo, R$ 1,4 milhão. O valor seria destinado ao FMDCA de Corumbá.

A sentença, no entanto, fixou a reparação em R$ 162,1 mil. Diante disso, o MPMS recorreu para tentar aumentar o valor da indenização.

Segundo o órgão, o montante definido na sentença não reflete adequadamente a gravidade e o impacto coletivo das condutas analisadas no processo.

MC Pipokinha é condenada por show com conteúdo sexual em MS — Foto: Divulgação

Doroth Helena de Sousa Alves, conhecida artisticamente como MC Pipokinha, tem 28 anos. A cantora catarinense cresceu em Tubarão (SC) e atualmente mora em São Paulo.

Ela ganhou destaque no funk de rua, conhecido como “mandelão”, com letras ousadas e apresentações marcadas por movimentos sexuais e interação com o público.

Entre as músicas que ajudaram a projetar a cantora estão “Bota na Pipokinha”, “Eu sou a MC Pipokinha” e “Tira as Crianças da Sala”.

articles.title: Rio Acre fica abaixo de 2 metros pela 3ª vez em 2026 na capital | G1
articles.standfirst: Manancial marcou 1,88 metros na medição das 5h de domingo (30). Todas as três marcas foram registradas em agosto. Falta de chuvas e calor contribuem para situação em Rio Branco.
articles.summary: Manancial marcou 1,88 metros na medição das 5h de domingo (30). Todas as três marcas foram registradas em agosto. Falta de chuvas e calor contribuem para situação em Rio Branco.
articles.body:
Pela terceira vez em 2026 , o Rio Acre ficou abaixo dos dois metros e chegou a 1,83 metros na medição das 5h desta segunda-feira (31), em Rio Branco . Este é o nível mais baixo já registrado este ano.

O mês de agosto foi marcado pela oscilação no nível do manancial. Na medição do último domingo (30), quando o rio voltou a ficar abaixo dos 2 metros, o nível marcou 1,88 metros , diminuindo 12 centímetros com relação a sábado (29), quando estava com exatos 2 metros. ( Veja o gráfico mais abaixo )

As três vezes que o manancial ficou abaixo desta marca, inclusive, foram registradas neste mês de agosto, sendo estas:

No dia 12, quando registrou 1,98 metros , permanecendo até o dia 16, quando voltou a subir e marcou 2 metros;

No dia 23, quando registrou 1,98 metros e voltou a subir no dia seguinte, marcando 2,20 metros;

No último domingo (29), ao alcançar a marca de 1,88 metros.

Pela terceira vez, Rio Acre fica abaixo de 2 metros na capital — Foto: Richard Lauriano/Rede Amazônica Acre

De acordo com o coordenador da Defesa Civil Municipal, tenente-coronel Cláudio Falcão, o nível registrado nesta segunda não ultrapassa outras marcas registradas em anos anteriores.

Porém, a situação não ameniza as situações de estiagem enfrentadas na capital, tendo em vista que as oscilações ocorreram devido às chuvas registradas em outras cidades do estado.

“Ou seja, não melhora em nada a nossa situação hídrica e seca que estamos vivendo com situação de emergência, inclusive. Então, é um nível baixo e nós já estamos em cota de alerta máximo há muito tempo . Quando ele baixou de 2,69 metros, já entramos nessa cota de alerta máxima e a gente continua, até a situação ficar bem mais complicada”, detalhou.

Ainda de acordo com o coordenador, a tendência é que o nível do Rio Acre continue a diminuir no mês de setembro. “Os recordes que foram batidos aconteceram sempre no mês de setembro e início de outubro. Então, a gente tem uns dias pela frente ainda para abaixar mais o nível ainda”, complementou.

Além disto, Falcão afirmou ainda que as altas temperaturas registradas no estado também tem influência na diminuição do nível do rio.

“É uma coisa que era previsível. Nós estamos com média de 36 graus por dia com sensação térmica até maior e, infelizmente, a tendência é que agora no mês de setembro esse calor aumente [...] e isso afeta diretamente todo o nosso bem-estar, nossa saúde, além de continuar deixando mais seco ainda toda a região e a diminuição dos rios. [...] O calor intenso causa evaporação e, em caso de represas, seca cada vez mais”, explicou.

O cenário atual contrasta com o registrado no início do ano, quando o Rio Acre chegou a ultrapassar a cota de transbordo em Rio Branco por duas vezes, sendo uma em 14 de janeiro e outra em 31 do mesmo mês . Na última enchente, inclusive, o manancial chegou a 15,44 metros e atingiu cerca de 12 mil pessoas.

Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil, não há previsões de muitas chuvas para os próximos meses.

“A previsão de chuvas é abaixo da média, para esses próximos meses mesmo, no plural, setembro, outubro, novembro e dezembro também. [...] Então, nós temos quatro meses, até virar o ano, de previsão de pouca chuva”, afirmou.

No dia 11 de agosto, a Prefeitura de Rio Branco decretou situação de emergência por causa da redução das chuvas e dos níveis dos rios, com risco de comprometimento do abastecimento de água. No início do mês, o governo também publicou o ato diante da possibilidade de desabastecimento hídrico.

O Brasil deve passar por ao menos seis ondas de calor nos próximos meses , segundo uma análise do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden). O fenômeno, que já foi mais concentrado em algumas regiões, hoje atinge o país inteiro ao mesmo tempo.

E mais: o número de ondas pode ser ainda maior, já que no último El Niño foram nove.

Uma onda de calor não é aquilo que ocorre em um dia quente, é muito mais do que isso. A onda acontece quando, por um período de pelo menos três dias seguidos , as temperaturas máximas e as mínimas ficam excepcionalmente acima do normal. Ou seja, não há trégua de calor.

A previsão aponta que vamos viver um Super El Niño, que pode entrar para os mais intensos já registrados. Ele deve trazer calor e seca, ao mesmo tempo em que provoca chuvas intensas com cenários diferentes pelas regiões do país. Mas há um consenso de norte a sul: o calor.

A estimativa parte de uma pesquisa que analisou o histórico de 47 anos de registros de temperaturas observando o fenômeno em anos de El Niño.

articles.title: Acidente na Raposo Tavares bloqueia acesso à SP-284 em Assis | G1
articles.standfirst: Parte da carga ficou espalhada na pista e causou o bloqueio total no km 447 da via, no acesso a SP-284. Motorista não se feriu no tombamento.
articles.summary: Acidente na Raposo Tavares com carreta de madeira bloqueia o acesso à SP-284 em Assis, exigindo desvios no trânsito após derramamento de carga na pista.
articles.body:
Carreta carregada com madeira tombou na rodovia entre Assis e Paraguaçu Paulista — Foto: Portal CCM/ Artesp

Uma carreta carregada com madeira tombou na manhã desta segunda-feira (31) na Rodovia Raposo Tavares entre Assis e Paraguaçu Paulista (SP).

Conforme a ocorrência, o veículo trafegava pela Rodovia SP-270, no sentido oeste, quando, na altura do km 447+080, ao acessar a alça que dá acesso a Rodovia Manílio Gobbi (SP-284), a carroceria tombou.

O acidente provocou o derramamento da carga sobre a pista, e o veículo permaneceu imobilizado no local. O motorista não se feriu.

Segundo informações da Agência Reguladora de Transporte de São Paulo (Artesp), com o derramamento da carga, a alça de acesso permanecia totalmente interditada até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Por causa da interdição total, os motoristas que pretendem acessar a SP-284, a orientação é utilizar o dispositivo de retorno pelo alço 500, sendo direcionados para o alça 650, com acesso à SP-270, no sentido leste. Na sequência, os motoristas devem acessar a alça 700, que dá acesso à SP-284.

articles.title: Tentativas de golpes por meios como mensagens ou ligações afetam 45 milhões no Brasil, diz pesquisa | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento aponta que aplicativos de mensagens, chamadas telefônicas e sites ou aplicativos falsos estão entre os meios mais usados por golpistas para abordar vítimas.
articles.summary: Levantamento aponta que aplicativos de mensagens, chamadas telefônicas e sites ou aplicativos falsos estão entre os meios mais usados por golpistas para abordar vítimas.
articles.body:
Ligações automáticas indesejadas, chamadas de "robocalls" — Foto: Fantástico

Uma pesquisa divulgada nesta segunda-feira (31) aponta que 32% dos brasileiros usuários de internet com 16 anos ou mais relatam já ter sofrido tentativas de golpes com uso de seus dados pessoais. O índice equivale a 45 milhões de pessoas.

Ainda segundo o levantamento, 20% dos usuários de internet com 16 anos ou mais afirmam ter sido, de fato, vítimas de golpes com uso de suas informações.

Os dados fazem parte da pesquisa Privacidade e Proteção de Dados Pessoais, realizada pelo Centro Regional de Estudos para o Desenvolvimento da Sociedade da Informação (Cetic.br), que ouviu 2.500 pessoas em dezembro de 2025.

Os meios mais usados por golpistas ao abordar vítimas são aplicativos de mensagens (84%), ligações (79%), sites ou aplicativos falsos (71%), SMS (71%), e-mail (69%) e redes sociais (67%).

Entre os que viveram situações envolvendo golpes, 48% afirmam que tiveram dinheiro roubado. No mesmo grupo, 43% dizem que perderam acesso a contas de e-mail ou de redes sociais.

Os usuários que foram alvos de golpistas também relatam ter sofrido mal-estar e estresse emocional (58%), dívidas feitas por terceiros (42%) e roubo de informações como números de cartões de crédito ou de senhas de banco (42%).

O levantamento aponta ainda que o tipo de dispositivo usado para acessar a internet pode aumentar a exposição a tentativas de golpes.

O uso de sites ou aplicativos falsos é mais comum contra usuários que navegam apenas pelo celular (80%) do que contra os que combinam o acesso móvel com o computador (68%), por exemplo.

Para o gerente do Cetic.br, Alexandre Barbosa, a pesquisa ajuda a comprovar que golpes envolvendo dados pessoais acontecem por diferentes canais e podem trazer consequências além das perdas financeiras.

"A disseminação dessas situações reforça a importância de iniciativas de prevenção e conscientização, combinadas a políticas de proteção de dados e segurança no ambiente digital", afirma.

articles.title: Míssil dos EUA utilizado pela 1ª vez no Irã deixou destruição e mortes | G1
articles.standfirst: Bombardeio com 3 projéteis PrSM, que explodem no ar e liberam esferas de metal, em Larmerd matou civis a 50 metros de distância do alvo no primeiro dia da guerra, segundo o Airwars.
articles.summary: Bombardeio com 3 projéteis PrSM, que explodem no ar e liberam esferas de metal, em Larmerd matou civis a 50 metros de distância do alvo no primeiro dia da guerra, segundo o Airwars.
articles.body:
Edifício e carro com diversos buracos após ataque aéreo em Lamerd, no sul do Irã, em 28 de fevereiro de 2026. — Foto: Alireza Ameri/Tasnim News Agency via AP

Um novo tipo de míssil, que explode e se fragmenta antes de tocar o solo, que foi utilizado pela 1ª vez em combate pelos Estados Unidos durante a guerra contra o Irã deixou um amplo rastro de destruição e dezenas de mortos, incluindo civis, segundo um relatório de um instituto especializado.

Os EUA lançaram três Mísseis de Ataque de Precisão (PrSM, na sigla em inglês) contra a cidade de Lamerd, no sul do Irã, no primeiro dia da guerra no Oriente Médio —no mesmo dia em que outro ataque com míssil Tomahawk matou centenas de crianças e professores em uma escola em Minab.

Esse ataque atingiu uma escola e um centro esportivo, e a composição desses mísseis amplificou o número de mortos e a destruição causada, segundo uma análise feita pelo do monitor de conflitos Airwars: foram pelo menos 21 civis mortos, incluindo sete crianças, e alguns deles estavam a 50 metros do ponto da explosão.

O PrSM foi projetado para explodir no ar e lançar dezenas de milhares de fragmentos metálicos densos em alta velocidade em todas as direções. O armamento é apresentado pelo seu fabricante como o míssil balístico do futuro, e diversos países como os EUA, Reino Unido e Austrália investiram bilhões de dólares para os acrescentar a seus arsenais.

Fotos, vídeos e imagens de satélite do local após os ataques em Lamerd, analisados pelo Airwars e verificados pela agência de notícias Associated Press (AP), mostram prédios, ruas e veículos fortemente marcados por impactos, em um padrão de explosão que, segundo especialistas, é compatível com as capacidades do PrSM. (Veja na foto acima)

O Airwars foi o primeiro a mapear o raio dos danos provocados pelo bombardeio com mísseis PrSM em Lamerd, seis meses após o início do conflito, e estimar o alcance letal da arma utilizada. A publicação do relatório evidencia para os riscos de utilizar um armamento de fragmentação contra áreas densamente povoadas.

As Forças Armadas dos EUA confirmaram ter lançado PrSMs contra o Irã e destacaram seu "primeiro uso na história" no ataque, porém negaram ter utilizado o armamento contra Lamerd. Ainda não havia sido esclarecido até a última atualização desta reportagem qual era o alvo pretendido no ataque em Lamerd, porque havia um complexo do da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã nas proximidades do ataque, porém imagens de satélite não mostraram danos no local.

Homem examina destroços de míssil após bombardeio em Lamerd, no Irã, em 28 de fevereiro de 2026. — Foto: Alireza Ameri/Tasnim News Agency via AP

Seis especialistas em armamentos, incluindo dois ex-integrantes das Forças Armadas, disseram à AP acreditar que de fato PrSMs foram utilizados para atingir Lamerd — e afirmaram ser improvável que armas israelenses ou iranianas tenham sido utilizadas. Todos disseram que as Forças Armadas deveriam evitar disparar o PrSM contra alvos próximos a áreas civis.

"Seria difícil encontrar uma justificativa para usar o PrSM em uma área densamente povoada", disse Michael Meier, ex-assessor do Exército dos EUA sobre as leis da guerra.

Em março, o governo Trump assinou um contrato com a fabricante Lockheed Martin para acelerar a entrega de mais mísseis PrSM.

Mísseis em Lamerd provocaram danos a grande distância dos pontos de explosão

Lançamento de Míssil de Ataque de Precisão (PrSM) dos Estados Unidos. Foto de abril de 2025. — Foto: Divulgação/Exército dos EUA

O Airwars encontrou imagens de uma escola em Lamerd que foi danificada pelo míssil que explodiu sobre o Complexo Esportivo Shahid Naimi, a cerca de 170 metros de distância.

A explosão matou sete civis, a maioria crianças, informou a imprensa estatal iraniana. O Airwars afirma ter utilizado material de código aberto para confirmar as mortes. Entre as vítimas estavam três adolescentes que jogavam vôlei e uma mulher que fumava narguilé em frente à sua casa.

Uma explosão separada sobre o bairro de Tal-e Khandagh matou Avina Barzegar, de 2 anos, que brincava no quintal de casa. O Airwars estima que o fragmento que atingiu Barzegar percorreu 50 metros desde o local da explosão. A organização chegou a essa conclusão ao geolocalizar a casa da menina com base em um vídeo que mostrava o portão de entrada e medir a distância até o ponto da explosão.

Nem o Airwars nem a AP encontraram relatos que indicassem a morte de militares ou integrantes das forças de segurança nos ataques, nem que instalações militares tenham sido atingidas.

articles.title: Mais de 60 seções eleitorais têm local de votação alterado no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudanças atingem 61 seções em 14 municípios. TRE orienta eleitores a consultar endereço e número da seção antes das eleições.
articles.summary: Mudanças atingem 61 seções em 14 municípios. TRE orienta eleitores a consultar endereço e número da seção antes das eleições.
articles.body:
Maior parte das mudanças ocorreu em Rio Branco, segundo o TRE — Foto: Iryá Rodrigues/g1

O Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Acre (TRE-AC) alterou o local de votação de 61 seções eleitorais em 14 municípios do estado para as Eleições 2026. A maior parte das mudanças ocorreu em Rio Branco, que teve 33 seções transferidas. (Veja a lista completa mais abaixo)

Segundo o órgão, as alterações foram feitas pela Justiça Eleitoral para melhorar as condições de funcionamento das seções e garantir 'conforto, segurança e acessibilidade aos eleitores'.

"A consulta prévia é importante mesmo para quem costuma votar há anos no mesmo endereço. Dessa forma, o eleitor evita descobrir somente no dia da eleição que houve mudança e reduz o risco de deslocamentos desnecessários, atrasos e outros transtornos", complementou o TRE.

A consulta pode ser feita pelo aplicativo e-Título ou pelo Autoatendimento Eleitoral, no site da Justiça Eleitoral. O eleitor também pode verificar diretamente os locais de votação disponibilizados pelo TRE-AC.

Rio Branco: 33 seções (26 da 1ª Zona Eleitoral e sete da 9ª Zona);

Porto Acre: 3 (duas da 1ª Zona e uma da 8ª);

A recomendação é que, além do endereço, o eleitor anote o número da seção. Com essa informação, poderá ir diretamente à sala onde estará instalada a urna, sem precisar procurar a seção dentro do prédio.

No primeiro turno, marcado para 4 de outubro, cada eleitor do Acre terá seis votos: para deputado federal, deputado estadual, duas vagas de senador, governador e presidente da República.

No Acre, as urnas funcionarão das 6h às 15h, no horário local. Caso haja segundo turno, a votação ocorre em 25 de outubro.

articles.title: As Bill Gates warns AI could wipe out jobs, US Senator Bernie Sanders backs him with a 5-word-warning; says: Congress must stand up to...
articles.summary: Tech News News: US Senator Bernie Sanders has thrown his weight behind Bill Gates once more, endorsing the Microsoft co-founder's warning that artificial intelligence.
articles.body: US Senator Bernie Sanders has thrown his weight behind Bill Gates once more, endorsing the Microsoft co-founder's warning that artificial intelligence poses a serious danger to jobs and to human life. Writing on X late Sunday night, the Vermont senator said Gates was right that AI "poses a grave threat to jobs and the future of humanity" and that dealing with the risks should be, in Gates's phrase, the world's top priority. He closed with a line in capitals: "WE MUST ACT BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE."The post landed days after Gates published a roughly 6,000-word essay on his personal site laying out three risks he believes the world is unprepared for: permanent job losses, AI-enabled bioterrorism and cyberattacks, and the effect of AI companions on children. Sanders added his own political framing to it, calling on Congress to stand up to what he described as the wealth and power of Big Tech oligarchs. The alignment is not new. Sanders first sided with Gates on taxing automation in his 2023 book, and returned to the theme in December, asking how displaced workers would pay rent or buy healthcare once the machines were doing the work.Bernie Sanders has been circling this argument since before ChatGPT went mainstreamSanders has never been shy about automation. His 2020 campaign promised to strip tax breaks from companies that swapped employees for robots. Earlier this month he went further, writing to the chief executives of Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic and asking them to pause frontier development outright. That letter cited reports of models being used to help design new viruses and of AI systems breaching other companies' servers, which Sanders read as evidence that the industry's own risk thresholds had already been crossed.Bill Gates wants a token tax and a list of jobs machines are not allowed to takeGates is not asking anyone to stop building. He has said he would support a credible global slowdown but does not believe one is coming, given the geopolitical and commercial pressure to keep going. His proposals are structural instead. He wants a tax on AI tokens and robots, on the logic that employers currently pay payroll tax on a human hire but can write off a machine immediately, and he wants the revenue funnelled into retraining and a wider safety net.He has also floated something he calls Human Reserved: categories of work set aside for people by decision rather than by economics. Caregiving is his example, drawn from watching paid carers look after his father in the final stages of Alzheimer's. In a recent interview he was blunter than his essay, saying tech executives privately understand how capable these systems are but avoid saying so publicly because of the trillions still to be raised. On the industry's preferred approach he was dismissive: self-regulation on the most dangerous tool ever invented, no thanks.The jobs data does not show a collapse yet, only a door closing on young workersNot everyone is convinced. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang pushed back last week, saying he loves Gates but does not see what Gates sees, and predicting AI will create work at unprecedented scale. The numbers so far sit awkwardly between them. AI was named in 112,713 announced US job cuts through July, about 24 percent of the total and the leading stated reason for five straight months, yet overall announced cuts are down 41 percent year on year.The sharper signal is generational. Stanford researchers tracking payroll data found employment among 22 to 25 year olds in heavily AI-exposed roles running 19 percent below where it should be. Sanders wants Congress moving before that becomes the whole labour market rather than its youngest edge.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: A San Antonio storm knocked out power and damaged homes; one barber simply moved his chair outside and kept cutting customers’ hair
articles.summary: US News: A powerful storm knocked out power and damaged homes across San Antonio on Friday night, but a barber refused to close his shop. Texas Publilc Radio r.
articles.body: A powerful storm knocked out power and damaged homes across San Antonio on Friday night, but a barber refused to close his shop. Texas Publilc Radio reported that with no electricity, he moved his barber chair outside and continued cutting customers’ hair as residents cleaned up fallen trees and dealt with the heat.Winds of 50 to 65 mph, heavy rain, lightning and flash flooding to parts of the city knocked down trees and power lines across the city, left homes damaged, trees and utility poles toppled and more than 112,000 CPS Energy customers without electricity at its peak.Tens of thousands of people were still without power on Saturday as residents began clearing debris and checking the damage. With temperatures rising towards 100 degrees, families without electricity also had to find ways to stay cool.On San Antonio’s West Side, the morning after the storm was filled with the sounds of chainsaws, generators and people working together. Streets near Zarzamora Street were covered with fallen branches and trees. Some trees had landed on homes and vehicles, while others brought down power lines.No electricity stops this barberThe power cuts also affected businesses across the West Side. Some businesses closed on Saturday, while others looked for ways to continue operating despite the outage.At the Misfit barbershop on Martin Street, owner and barber Juan Martinez decided not to close. Instead, he moved a barber’s chair outside the shop and continued cutting customers’ hair.The chair was placed beneath an awning, where it had some shade. The shop itself had no electricity, but Martinez was determined to keep working. “It’s a hard time, but you want to look good,” Martinez said.For Martinez, closing was not really an option. “I’m a business owner and as long as I’m out here showing my guys, power, no power, we can still do it,” he said.A little wind outside was enough to make the arrangement possible, Martinez said. His customers were also trying to deal with the situation in the same way.“It’s hard, it’s crazy, it’s difficult, but at the end of the day all they say is we gotta roll with the punches. We gotta keep positive.”The damage around the neighbourhood was still clearly visible. Fallen trees had hit vehicles and power lines, while some homes had roofs badly damaged or completely removed.“These trees are old and you see them and the trees are knocked over the vehicles, knocked out powerlines, there’s a couple of houses where the roofs are caved in, roofs are taken off, it’s just madness right now,” Martinez said.West Side residents help each otherDespite the damage and power outages, Martinez said the neighbourhood had an important strength- its community. “I feel like as a community we can pull together,” he said.Martinez was born and raised on the West Side and said the area’s history and roots were an important part of its identity.“That’s what I love about the West Side,” he said. “I’m born and raised over here. The West Side has history. You have roots down here. You have a foundation of who you are.”Residents spent Saturday dealing with the immediate effects of the storm. Some cut up fallen trees, others cleared damaged homes, while families without electricity tried to stay cool.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani goes to court to stop a law passed by New York City Council to give $10,000 bonuses to teachers that he supported during election campaign
articles.summary: Tech News News: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has filed a lawsuit to stop a law passed by the New York City Council granting one-time $10,000 bonuses to low-paid.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has filed a lawsuit to stop a law passed by the New York City Council granting one-time $10,000 bonuses to low-paid school aides, known as paraprofessionals. The move marks a surprising break with the United Federation of Teachers (UFT), which endorsed Mamdani in last year’s mayoral election and had his support for the bonuses during the campaign. According to a report by the Wall Street Journal, the City Council unanimously passed the legislation in late July, covering around 25,000 school aides whose salaries start at $32,000. Mamdani allowed the bill to become a law without veto but sued days later, arguing the bonuses would cost the city $325 million and violate collective bargaining rules. His lawsuit asserts that compensation must be determined through negotiations between unions and the mayor, not legislation, warning that the council’s move sets a precedent for bypassing bargaining.What the bonuses passed by the New York City Council would coverThe bonuses passed by New York City Council covered roughly 25,000 city school aides who are also known as paraprofessionals, who typically work with students with special needs and whose salaries start at around $32,000. In July this year, the City Council unanimously agreed also passed a legislation granting these workers one-time $10,000 payments. At that time, Mamdani also chose not to veto the bill, allowing it to automatically become law. However, later Mamdani sue the council in state court, arguing the bonuses would cost the city an estimated $325 million.Zohran Mamdani’s legal argumentIn pursuing the lawsuit, Mamdani is asserting his executive authority over labor-contract negotiations. The suit argues that the bonuses violate a decades-old law requiring that compensation be determined through collective bargaining between unions and the mayor's office, not through City Council legislation. According to the lawsuit, allowing the bonus law to stand would set a troubling precedent, opening a path for unions to secure pay increases that bypass the traditional give-and-take of contract negotiations entirely.Why the council moved forward anywayCity Council Speaker Julie Menin, a Democrat, said the council had hoped Mamdani would negotiate pay raises for paraprofessionals directly or include salary increases in this year's budget. When neither happened, the council proceeded with its own legislation. Menin argued the aides are underpaid, and that raising their salaries would help fill the roughly 1,600 current vacancies in the role while lowering education costs over the long run. She framed the raise as both ethically and fiscally sound.UFT President Michael Mulgrew, whose union represents 200,000 members, said in a statement that the council's legislation was necessary to address chronic workforce shortages and was designed in a way that legally protects the collective bargaining process. Mulgrew had earlier warned, in a New York Times interview this summer, that he would wage an "all-out war" if Mamdani tried to block the legislation. His union filed a motion this week to formally intervene in the court case.The Mayor's office respondsA mayoral spokesman said the administration filed the lawsuit to keep negotiations between the city and its workforce centered at the bargaining table rather than being decided through political intervention. The spokesman added that Mamdani's office has been in active talks with the teachers union to address fair compensation for school aides.A Zohran Mamdani caught between principle and precedentAs per the WSJ report, Evan Stone, chief executive of the teacher-led advocacy group Educators for Excellence, described the council's legislation as putting Mamdani in a genuinely difficult position. According to Stone, Mamdani agrees in principle that school aides deserve higher pay, but feels he needs to defend the traditional process for setting citywide compensation — historically, mayors have relied on pattern bargaining to apply a standard percentage raise across city union contracts, avoiding a situation where one group receives a disproportionately large increase relative to others.Stone said allowing this particular bonus to stand could call the entire historical bargaining process into question at a moment when the city is already facing tight budget constraints. He also acknowledged the political risk to Mamdani, noting that some teachers who supported his campaign may feel frustrated that he hasn't followed through on a promise he backed as a candidate.Michael Petrilli, president of the education reform think tank Thomas B. Fordham Institute, said this kind of rift between a Democratic politician and teachers unions is notable, since conventional political wisdom generally holds that Democratic officials try to avoid conflict with such an important part of their political base.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Sir James Cleverly accuses Andy Burnham of 'war on London'
articles.summary: Sir James Cleverly resigned from the shadow cabinet on Saturday to run for mayor of London.
articles.body:
Sir James Cleverly, who resigned from the shadow cabinet on Saturday to run for mayor of London, has accused the prime minister of waging a "war on London" and pursuing a "very anti-London agenda".

The senior Conservative claimed Andy Burnham's devolution drive would come at the expense of London, arguing the plans centralised power in Manchester.

On Saturday, Sir James announced he was quitting the Tory front bench as shadow secretary of state for housing, communities and local government to run for City Hall at the next mayoral election in 2028.

A government spokesperson said devolution plans would "deliver good growth in every postcode".

The Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan, is halfway through his third term and has neither confirmed nor ruled out standing again.

Speaking to LBC on Sunday, Sir James said Burnham was "stripping hundreds of millions of pounds out of the budget of London councils".

The government's fairer funding review, launched while Sir Keir Starmer was Labour leader, could see some London councils face cuts to their funding settlements as part of a bid to redirect money to more deprived areas.

The government has defended the changes, arguing it is "fixing an outdated funding system" where some of the wealthiest parts of the country "benefited from exceptionally high levels of government support, while communities facing greater pressures lost out".

Sir James, the MP for Braintree in Essex, said Burnham was "blaming London for London's own success".

He added: "The UK cannot be successful as a country unless London is successful as a city. And I see this in Braintree.

"Andy Burnham just doesn't get it.... He's got a war with London, and London needs someone to fight its corner."

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said they were working with local leaders across the country, including in London, to deliver "good growth".

"This isn't about boosting other cities at the expense of the capital – London and all other places with mayors benefit from the set of devolved powers and budgets on offer as we continue to shift power away from Westminster and back to local people," they said.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has initiated proceedings to seal a playschool in Maujpur where a 3-year-old boy was allegedly assaulted, the chief minister’s office said on Monday.The action was taken on the directions of chief minister Rekha Gupta, news agency PTI reported.The district magistrate has initiated proceedings to seal the premises, while the police investigation into the incident is underway.“Delhi government has taken serious cognisance of the deeply disturbing incident reported from a play school in Maujpur,” the CMO said in a post on X.The government said it would ensure that responsibility is fixed and those found guilty face the strictest action under the law.Police have registered a case invoking sections of the POCSO Act and others under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the school director, principal, teacher and a caretaker, with the latter arrested.Police have medically examined the child at GTB Hospital, PTI reported.The child's family alleged that he was beaten up at school and subjected to inappropriate conduct.According to the family, they suspected abuse after noticing changes in the child's behaviour, including alleged difficulty sleeping and fear of using the toilet.The case had earlier prompted scrutiny of the school after the child’s family alleged that he had also been physically assaulted.CCTV footage examined by police purportedly showed the child being tied to a chair, kicked and held by his ears. articles.title: Israel’s far-right competes for votes with increasingly extreme visions
articles.summary: Far-right Israeli minister Itamar Ben Gvir has made it a point to post videos of himself on social media taunting or mocking Palestinian prisoners. He boasted of threatening the most high-profile Palestinian prisoner. He showed off activists from a Gaza flotilla bound on the floor. And he is proud of a new law he pushed to expand the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of terrorism.
articles.body: Far-right Israeli minister Itamar Ben Gvir has made it a point to post videos of himself on social media taunting or mocking Palestinian prisoners. He boasted of threatening the most high-profile Palestinian prisoner. He showed off activists from a Gaza flotilla bound on the floor. And he is proud of a new law he pushed to expand the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of terrorism. But as elections near, his messaging has grown more extreme. His latest AI-generated campaign video shows rows of numbered Palestinian prisoners in brown uniforms moving along a conveyor belt into a fenced compound with watchtowers; the inmates appear well-fed at the start and thinner and distressed after passing through the industrial-style processing line. The post says, “We promised - we delivered.” The video was removed from Ben Gvir’s account on X after amassing more than 4 million views. The minister has long called for conditions of Palestinian security prisoners to be reduced to “the minimum required by law.” Ben Gvir is perhaps the best known of Israel’s far-right politicians, a provocateur with his hands on the country’s levers of power. As the minister of National Security, he is in charge of the police and the prisons as his politics have become a defining feature of Israel’s image abroad. With two months until the elections, Israel’s far-right field is becoming increasingly crowded, packed with small parties vying for a finite pool of votes. To stand out, politicians are unabashed in their messaging and their vision for the country. The far-right is a dominant feature in Israeli politics – and a key component of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition. Political parties need to garner 3.25% of the vote to cross the electoral threshold and enter the next parliament. Those that fall short are excluded, and their votes effectively thrown out. That electoral arithmetic is intensifying competition for right-wing voters and pushing politicians to adopt even harder-line positions. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich repeatedly celebrates the expansion of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, openly boasting of destroying the possibility of a Palestinian state. A cornerstone of his election campaign is called “Yes. Let’s Judaize!” – a plan which aims to change the demographic reality in the Negev and Galilee, areas of Israel with substantial Arab populations, by applying settlement strategies from the West Bank: bringing a million additional Jewish residents and establishing about 40 new communities alongside dozens of individual farms. Meanwhile, Ofer Winter recently launched his new “Your People Israel” party. The retired brigadier general is popular among Israel’s right-wing and religious Zionist movement. At the party’s launch event in late-August, he said, “There will never be a Palestinian state here. The solution in Gaza is simple – emigration.” His party’s number two is Yoseph Haddad, an Arab Christian who is a pro-Israel activist and provocateur. Haddad, who has set his sights on becoming the minister of Public Diplomacy in the next government and the first Arab member of the Security Cabinet, said, “It is time the Arab community has representatives who work for them, not for Gaza, Jenin, and Ramallah. I hold them in contempt.” Avi Maoz, who leads the far-right “Noam” party, has railed against gay Pride parades in Jerusalem, secularism, and feminism. On his own, he is not expected to cross the electoral threshold. Nor is Moshe Feiglin’s “Identity” party. Feiglin, a veteran far-right libertarian political activist and occasional member of Netanyahu’s Likud party, has advocated for the destruction of Gaza and the “voluntary” emigration of Palestinians to third countries. “Every child in Gaza is the enemy,” he said last year on Israel’s Channel 14. “We need to occupy Gaza and settle it, and not a single Gazan child will be left there.” For Netanyahu, the abundance of far-right parties creates a real risk of losing tens of thousands of votes. If any of these parties fall under the electoral threshold, Netanyahu has warned that the right-wing risks losing the election. The prime minister has released several video and social media messages in recent weeks, publicly pleading with Ben Gvir, Smotrich and Winter to unite as one bloc instead of running as smaller parties. But so far, the right-wing parties are focusing on their own campaigns and leaning into a message that is becoming more extreme.

articles.title: The John Galliano 2027 Met Gala has been canceled
articles.summary: The exhibit was scrapped amid a growing outcry over the decision to honor the controversial British designer.
articles.body: John Galliano, the controversial British designer, will no longer be the subject of an exhibit linked to the Met Gala at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the museum said in a statement Monday. The move comes after a growing outcry over the decision by the museum and Anna Wintour, global editorial director of Vogue, to honor the designer at the Met Gala. Galliano was fired from Dior in 2011 and found guilty of “public insults” based on origin, religion, race or ethnicity after videos emerged of the designer saying “I love Hitler” and ranting antisemitic abuse at a café in Paris. The Met Gala, which is held on the first Monday in May, would fall next year on Yom HaShoah, a day of Holocaust remembrance. “After much reflection and discussion with all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” Galliano wrote in a statement released Monday. “I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry.” Galliano did “not want the debate surrounding me to place the Met in a difficult position or to distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute,” the statement continued. Andrew Bolton, the curator of the Met’s Costume Institute, said in a statement issued by the museum that he recognized “the pain and concern this exhibition has caused.” He continued: “After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed.” Wintour, who is also chief content officer at Condé Nast and has spearheaded the organization of the Met Gala since 1995, said that Galliano’s decision to pull out of the showcase was “very courageous and a measure of the man he is.” “I believe this is the right decision,” Wintour said. “John Galliano: Horizons” was supposed to “consider how artistic achievement should be understood alongside ethical accountability,” read a press release from the museum announcing the exhibit just a few weeks ago. But the decision sparked outrage, particularly outside of the fashion industry, and trustees as well as members of the museum’s board were “scrambling to do damage control,” the New York Times reported this weekend, ahead of the Monday announcement. This is not the first time the Met Gala has been at the center of controversy. When the late Karl Lagerfeld was announced as the subject for the Costume Institute exhibition in 2023, his problematic comments disparaging the #MeToo movement, refugees and plus-sized bodies were resurfaced as evidence against his celebration. Earlier this year, the Met Gala faced another torrent of backlash when it was announced that Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez Bezos would be the main benefactors of the event. The news was met with calls for boycotts, and alternative events were staged around New York City, highlighting the safety issues at Amazon warehouses and growing wealth inequality. Galliano, whose designs have achieved cult status in the industry and are often lauded for their theatricality and detail, would have been just the third living fashion designer awarded a Met retrospective, after Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017 and Yves Saint Laurent in 1983. “Does he deserve it as a person? Questionable,” said Dana Thomas, who wrote the 2015 biography “Gods and Kings” about Galliano and Alexander McQueen. “Does he deserve it as a designer? Absolutely.” Thomas also underscored the professional risk Bolton faced by staging the Galliano exhibition in the first place: “Nobody will ever take what he does seriously again if he doesn’t pull this off.”

articles.title: Jim Clyburn regrets supporting Clarence Thomas' SCOTUS appointment, calling it a 'mistake'
articles.summary: Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C., called supporting Clarence Thomas during his 1991 confirmation hearing a "mistake," saying the justice rebelled against his background.
articles.body: Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C., told NBC News' "Meet the Press" on Sunday that he regretted supporting Clarence Thomas during his 1991 Supreme Court confirmation hearing, calling it a "mistake." During the show, host Kristen Welker remarked that Clyburn had previously testified in favor of Thomas' appointment to the Supreme Court during his contentious 1991 hearing. Since his appointment, Thomas has been considered a prominent conservative justice. Welker asked Clyburn whether he stood by his decision to support Thomas as the Democratic Party increasingly supports court-packing and enforcing term limits for justices. CLARENCE THOMAS PRAISED AFTER RARE TELEVISED ADDRESS WARNING OF PROGRESSIVISM GOES VIRAL "Absolutely not. I have made mistakes in my life," Clyburn said. "And that’s one that I made, and I will own up to that mistake. The fact of the matter is, I had faith and confidence in the fact that his background and experiences would instruct him in his professionalism, especially sitting on the bench. We had worked together when he was chair of the Equal [Employment] Opportunity Commission and, of course, I was running the state agency here in South Carolina." Clyburn said that, despite their political differences, he believed that Thomas would be "upholding those precedents" set by the Voting Rights Act and Civil Rights Act. "I had no idea that Clarence Thomas would rebel the way he has against his own background and experiences. He was raised by his grandfather, and he has shown very little sensitivity to the environment his grandfather grew up in Pin Point, Georgia," Clyburn said. During the 1991 hearing, Clyburn referred to Thomas as "a personal and professional friend, in spite of the fact that he shares a conservative Republican philosophy." By Sunday, however, he referred to Thomas as a "very angry rightist." 'LOOK AT ME!' JUSTICE FIRES BACK AT CRITICS WHO DARE QUESTION HIS BLACKNESS "I had hoped that Clarence Thomas would follow the modern underpinnings of that Constitution of ours, but he has not done so," Clyburn said. "In fact, he decided to go all the way from an angry leftist to a very angry rightist." During a rare interview with Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz last week, Thomas rejected the idea that being a Black man requires him to subscribe to Democratic beliefs. "We had this saying [that there are] only two things I have to do: stay Black and die," Thomas said. articles.title: Nepal tragedy: Owners missing, dog refuses to leave flood-hit Trishuli home
articles.summary: South Asia News: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT): A black-and-white dog, its collar still intact, has refused to leave the site of a row of four homes washed away in last we.
articles.body: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT): A black-and-white dog, its collar still intact, has refused to leave the site of a row of four homes washed away in last week's flood in Trishuli Bazaar, remaining in the same muddy patch even as half a dozen JCBs and rescue workers clear timber, silt and debris around him. He barely reacts to strangers, does not wag his tail at all and keeps returning to what used to be the front entrance of one of the houses.Volunteer relief worker Bikram Thapa told TOI that workers initially tried offering biscuits and calling him by common pet names. “We’ve tried coaxing him with biscuits and calling him by all sorts of pet names, but he doesn't even turn his head. His collar is intact,” he said. “He won't leave this place.”Sunil Tamang, who has been working on debris clearance, said even the roar of heavy machinery operating only metres away failed to move the dog. “In the middle of all the heavy JCB engines and clearing operations, he just sits in that muddy pool,” Tamang told TOI. “Not a single wag of his tail. He refuses to cross the boundary of where his yard used to end.”Tamang said the dog showed no panic even when excavators moved close to the spot. He would occasionally lift his head at the sound of an approaching vehicle or people moving through the debris, but then settle back in the same place once they passed.The dog’s home, like the rest of the small neighbourhood around it, no longer exists. The flood washed away the row of houses and erased familiar boundaries, leaving only mud, debris and scattered remains of structures. Nobody working at the site could identify his owners or say which of the four homes he belonged to, but his repeated return to the same former doorway and refusal to move beyond what used to be the yard suggested this had been his territory.Community animal rescue volunteer Rita Gurung said workers eventually stopped trying to make him leave and instead began placing dry food and water nearby. “We keep leaving dry rations near him every few hours,” Gurung told TOI. “He only takes a bite when the road is quiet.”Displaced resident Maya Adhikari said most dogs in the area moved towards higher ground when the flood struck, but this one stayed around the destroyed houses. “This was his territory, his family's courtyard,” she said.Local shopkeeper Dinesh Basyal said residents who had themselves lost homes had begun watching out for him. “We lost our homes, but we understand what happened,” Basyal said. “He doesn't understand why everyone disappeared — he just knows he isn't supposed to leave until they return.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Why has Greece signed a $3.5bn missile deal with Israel?
articles.summary: Analysts say Greece is concerned about threats posed by the US-Israel war on Iran and Turkiye’s growing capabilities.
articles.body:
Greece has inked a weapons deal with Israel that will see a $3.5bn multi-layered air defence system delivered to Athens in what is the largest defence agreement ever between the two countries.

The agreement, signed on Monday in Tel Aviv, comes as Greece’s relations with its neighbour and rival, Turkiye, have grown more sour. It also, however, breaks with a broader European wariness of being seen as too close to Israel, following the genocidal war on Gaza and Israel’s increasingly blatant efforts to annex the occupied West Bank.

Greece and Israel have long shared economic and diplomatic ties. They’ve also regularly conducted joint military exercises.

The new purchase is part of Greece’s plans to modernise its military by 2030. Athens will spend about 28 billion euros ($32bn) by 2036 to build the Israeli defence system, known collectively in Greece as the Achilles Shield, as well as to buy up to 40 F-35 fighter jets from the United States and frigates from France and Italy.

Achilles Shield, which was negotiated over three years, will be delivered in stages. It is scheduled to reach full operational readiness within 35 months.

According to a statement by the Israeli Ministry of Defence, the Achilles Shield comprises three core systems:

David’s Sling is developed by the Israeli Missile Defense Organization. It’s an advanced air and missile defence system designed to intercept tactical ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and medium-to-long-range rockets through direct kinetic impact. It travels at supersonic speed and can engage threats from 40km to 300km (25 miles to 185 miles) away.

The Spyder is manufactured by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. This surface-to-air missile system is designed to engage low-altitude aerial threats like aircraft, helicopters, drones and guided munitions.

The Barak MX multi-modal defence system is manufactured by Israel Aerospace Industries. It can engage a wider spectrum of threats, including cruise missiles, ballistic missiles, fighter jets, helicopters, and unmanned aerial vehicles, from 35km to 150km (55 miles to 240 miles) away using four models of interceptors.

As part of the deal, Israel will also deliver multi-mission radars for air surveillance, as well as an artificial intelligence-enabled command centre incorporating all the technologies.

A statement by an Israeli Defence Ministry spokesperson also added that a supplementary deal valued at 26 million euros ($30m) would see Israel sell Greece drone dome systems as well.

Analysts say Greece is increasingly concerned about threats posed by the US-Israel war on Iran, especially as Tehran has launched strikes on US allies in the Gulf.

“One needs to be aware that Greece is the host of American naval bases and those might become in the future a target for the Iranians,” Wolfgang Pusztai, a security policy analyst who formerly served as an Austrian defence attache in Greece, told Al Jazeera.

“This is a capability that Greece and other European countries might need in the case that Iran is threatening them, too,” he added, referring to the defence systems.

While the US’s Patriot defence system is highly coveted, several European nations have been turning to Israel’s David Sling, which is cheaper and more effective, Pusztai said. The US itself is also running critically low on Patriots. In May, Switzerland was informed that a Patriot’s delivery from the US would be delayed and would be more expensive amid the war on Iran.

Greece is also wary of Turkiye’s increasing drone capabilities, analysts say. Ankara and Athens have long sparred over maritime boundaries, including control over disputed areas in the Aegean Sea and the Eastern Mediterranean. Tensions between Turkiye and Israel are also rising over Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

“This is certainly a reason why [Greece] will deploy the first elements of the Achilles Shield in the Aegean,” Pusztai added.

Turkiye has not yet reacted to the new defence deal. The growing military relationship between Greece, Israel and Cyprus – with which Turkiye also has territorial tensions – has previously drawn negative reactions from Ankara.

“We’re already hearing some Turkish analysts talking to Turkish media about how Greece’s weapons procurement deal from Israel makes Greece effectively co-responsible for everything that Israel does in the occupied West Bank and Gaza,” Al Jazeera’s John Psaropoulos said from Athens.

Cyprus, in December, was the first to buy Israel’s Barak defence system.

Turkish defence commentators at the time condemned the purchase.

“The Greek Cypriot administration has now become a complete proxy for the US and Israel,” said Cem Gurdeniz, a prominent retired rear admiral and a major proponent of Turkiye’s “Blue Homeland” maritime doctrine, which asserts Ankara’s sovereignty over large swaths of disputed areas in the Aegean, Black, and Eastern Mediterranean seas.

What is the reaction to Israel in Greece?

As in several European countries, many people in Greece are opposed to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and to deepening ties with Israel.

About 76 percent of Greeks do not believe Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will do the right thing regarding world affairs, according to a Pew Research Center poll released in June.

Opposition figures and intellectuals have loudly criticised Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis’s strengthening relations with Israel, and have accused Israel of seeking to use their country as a proxy.

“The transformation of Greece into an Israeli satellite is proceeding at breakneck speed,” Greece’s former Finance Minister Yanis Varoufakis posted on X last week. “This bodes ill for the majority of Greeks, for peace in our region and for Europe and West Asia more broadly. It must be resisted.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shakes hands with Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis during a joint press conference in West Jerusalem, December 22, 2025 [Abir Sultan/Reuters]

articles.title: Trump says Iran is ‘dead’, vows to respond after renewed clashes
articles.summary: US president promises to hit Iran and calls for the country’s leaders to be prosecuted for killing protesters.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has once again declared that Iran is “dead”, calling for the country’s leaders to be tried for what he described as “war crimes against humanity”.

Trump also promised on Monday to respond to the recent Iranian attack on a base hosting US troops in Jordan.

The US president’s outburst came as the US-Israel war on Iran entered its seventh month amid renewed clashes and no end in sight.

“Iran is officially a Failed Nation,” Trump wrote in a social media post. “IT IS DEAD! They have no Navy, they have no Air Force, they have no currency, they are not paying their soldiers or police, Inflation is at 300%, and their leadership is in total disarray and incapable of properly representing the country.”

Trump has been reiterating since the early days of the conflict that the Iranian governing system is collapsing. But the regime has remained standing without any major defections, with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spearheading the war effort.

Fighting in the region restarted on Sunday after the US military struck Iran’s Larak Island , saying it targeted launchers preparing to fire rockets carrying naval mines at the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran was quick to retaliate, launching missiles at a base that hosts US troops in Jordan, demonstrating the ability and willingness to strike back when attacked.

Trump vowed on Monday to respond to the Iranian response, a move that risks prolonging the clashes.

“We’re going to hit them hard,” the US president told Fox News. “There will be a response.”

The flare-up was the first round of fighting between the two countries since July.

The Trump administration had said it was shifting tactics from military operations to economic pressure.

But the latest skirmish showed that the risk of fighting remains high without an agreement to permanently end the war.

On Monday, Trump suggested that Iran’s crackdown on anti-government demonstrators is what is preventing the regime from collapsing.

“The only thing they have is FAKE NEWS from the USA, a willingness to kill their protesters (now over 100,000 people dead. They must be tried for war crimes against humanity!), and a good line of ‘BULL****,'” the US president wrote.

An alleged death toll of 100,000 protesters is a new record cited by Trump. The US president previously accused Iran of killing as many as 60,000 people during demonstrations earlier this year.

It is not clear how the US president came to the new number.

Iranian authorities have put the figure at 3,117, including members of the security forces, blaming the deaths on what it said were Israel-backed “rioters”.

Trump also appears to have combined war crimes – violations of the laws of war – with crimes against humanity, systemic campaigns of abuse against a civilian population.

Separately, Trump has imposed sanctions on International Criminal Court officials for issuing an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over war crime charges in Gaza.

Iran has also accused the US of committing war crimes and targeting civilians during the war. A strike on Minab, southern Iran, on the first day of the conflict hit a girls’ school, killing 168 people, mostly children.

articles.title: Grand Canyon search continues for 15 missing after flash flood destruction, two deaths
articles.summary: Federal and state authorities on Monday were still searching for some 15 missing hikers and backpackers after a devastating flash flood pummeled through the lower edge of the Grand Canyon over the weekend, killing at least two people.
articles.body: Federal and state authorities on Monday were still searching for some 15 missing hikers and backpackers after a devastating flash flood pummeled through the lower edge of the Grand Canyon over the weekend, killing at least two people. The National Park Service and local rescue agencies were conducting their search after evacuating dozens of visitors by Sunday, including several who were rescued by helicopter from a remote section of the park that is inaccessible by vehicle. The ramped-up search efforts come as authorities braced for another round of potentially ruinous climate conditions, officials said. The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered from Crystal Rapids on the Colorado River, the park service said Sunday evening. Officials have not released his name. It was not immediately clear when the second body was found. That victim’s details were not released. About 7 million people were under a flood watch Monday, covering a massive swath of the Southwest from southern Arizona to northern Colorado. The area at risk includes the Grand Canyon and stretches west into Utah, according to current weather projections. The most severe threat of flooding was in an area just north of the Grand Canyon. Phantom Ranch, a historic lodge at the bottom of Grand Canyon National Park, and a nearby trail were considered primary danger zones after the flooding. Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground and a large section of the North Kaibab Trail were closed on Monday, and as much as 40% of the Transcanyon Waterline had been impacted, officials said. The 12 ½-mile pipeline is the park’s main water supply system and much of it was damaged or destroyed. Administrators said there was damage to the Transcanyon Waterline “leaving the park with limited water reserves.” As a result, campgrounds were without water, and fires were prohibited starting Monday. “Visitors and residents are asked to conserve water as the park assesses flood damage and works to stabilize the water system,” NPS wrote on X. Park service officials said that all footbridges along Bright Angel Creek were destroyed in the major flooding event that began Saturday, eliminating all crossings for hikers. Campsites and hiking paths in the vicinity were closed until further notice. Images show rivers of muddy water barreling through lowlands, carrying cabins away from campsites, along with branches and other debris. Evacuated visitors were still reeling from the experience. David Gregory told NBC News that he crossed a footbridge to safety from Phantom Ranch before the structure was wrecked by the flooding. He was then airlifted out of the area. “It was kind of crazy hearing after that the bridge that we crossed was wiped out, kind of makes you think that maybe we should have been in more of a panic,” he said after he was taken to safety with about 50 others. Another video showed a male visitor on a footbridge marveling at the natural disaster under his feet. “We’re cooked!” the man said. The park service was asking for the public’s assistance in identifying anyone who may have been traveling through the affected area. “My heart is with the families and loved ones of every person unaccounted for after the flash flooding at the Grand Canyon,” Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs wrote on X. Hobbs said that the state Department of Emergency and Military Affairs and Coconino County Emergency Management were assisting the park service in its search.

articles.title: John Galliano exhibition at New York's Met cancelled after backlash
articles.summary: The exhibition faced criticism over the British fashion designer's conviction for making antisemitic remarks in 2011.
articles.body:
John Galliano has cancelled an upcoming major exhibition celebrating his work as a fashion designer after it prompted criticism due to his previous conviction for making antisemitic remarks.

The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York had announced an exhibition titled John Galliano: Horizons that was due to open in May 2027.

But Galliano said on Monday: "After much reflection and discussion with the Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time."

The British designer was sacked as creative director of Dior in 2011 and found guilty of abusing a Jewish curator in a restaurant in Paris.

A court also heard that he hurled racist insults at her friend, who is of South Asian origin, and in a separate incident declared a love for Hitler.

At the time, he apologised for his behaviour and his lawyer blamed it on "work-related stress and multiple addictions".

Galliano said in his statement on Monday: "I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it.

"I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture.

"It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one's conduct over time."

Galliano added that he did not want "to distract from the remarkable work" of the Met's Costume Institute and said he recognised and respected that "an exhibition honouring my work would be painful for some".

Galliano's new statement noted his "15 years of sobriety and recovery from alcoholism and addiction".

As well as being the focus of the exhibition, Galliano and his work in fashion would have provided the theme for the next Met Gala.

The star-studded event is due to take place on 3 May, coinciding with Yom HaShoah (Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day).

Vogue global editorial director Anna Wintour, a trustee of the Met and co-chair of the Met Gala, gave her support to Galliano on Monday.

"John's decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is," she said.

"I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support."

Others had previously voiced their opposition to the Met's plan to commemorate Galliano.

Julie Menin, speaker of New York City Council, said : "After my numerous and lengthy meetings and conversations with the Met, I am pleased that they have agreed to not honour John Galliano.

"From the beginning, I have told them that I strongly disagreed with this decision, and at this rising time of antisemitism, it had served as a gut punch to the Jewish community.

"This is the correct decision, as the harm and pain this was causing was simply unacceptable."

Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenblatt, chief executive of the Anti-Defamation League, which aims to counter antisemitism, said that with antisemitism at "crisis levels", honouring Galliano would be "misguided".

"Even Galliano ultimately recognised what the Met should have done from the start," he added. "This was the wrong move at the wrong moment. Timing matters."

Galliano is regarded by some as one of the greatest fashion designers and returned to the fashion industry following his conviction, serving as creative director of Margiela for a decade until 2024.
